newsitem.title: UK: UK department stores to see improving sales-report.
newsitem.headline: UK department stores to see improving sales-report.

text.p: British department stores could see sales up 10 percent in 1996/97 as they benefit from increased expenditure on household goods and investment in improving stores, a report published on Monday by Corporate Intelligence on Retailing said.
"The department store sector is now one of the fastest-growing retail markets in the UK," the UK retailing publication said in a statement.
"The top 50 department store groups increased their sales by 5.7 percent to 5.24 billion pounds in 1995/96, with an acceleration to almost 10 percent estimated for 1996/97," the statement said.

It said department stores, which had struggled in the 1970s and 1980s, are now "enjoying something of a renaissance as 'destination stores' and are regarded as essential anchors for new shopping developments.
Smaller groups could come under pressure from larger chains, the report warned.
The number of departments store outlets operated by the top ten chains has fallen to 224 in 1996 from 237 in 1991 but the recent upturn has encouraged some of the major chains to open new outlets.

"The main emphasis will be on improving returns from existing outlets and...department stores stand to gain from the rising numbers of older shoppers, who form their core target market," the statement said.
Corporate Intelligence on Retailing said people aged over 45 were expected to account for 46.2 percent of the population by 2020 compared with 38.3 percent in 1995.
The statement said department stores were in a position to reap the rewards of investment in stores during the 1980s and 1990s and could also improve sales density.
"Debenhams and House of Fraser, particularly, have scope for substantial improvement," the statement said.
